..
A westerly monsoon push is expected to continue bringing heavier
showers and thunderstorms to the Marianas, especially to Tinian and
Saipan overnight. After, a convergence zone is expected to shift
farther south, bringing higher shower and thunder coverage to Guam
and Rota Tuesday. Once TS Peilou (formerly Kujira) shoots to the
north and away from the Marianas and another disturbance begins
consolidating northeast of Pohnpei, a diffusive southwesterly flow is
expected to develop across the region. This will allow a dry spell 
to return, lasting until at least the weekend.

Marine...
Moderate to strong westerlies will prevail across the Marianas
tonight, will drop to gentle to fresh in Guam and Rota coastal
waters Tuesday, allowing seas to fall below 10 feet. As such, the
Small Craft Advisory is expected to expire late tonight for Guam
and Rota waters. Various significant northerly swells and large 
localized wind waves, are expected to continue producing sea 
conditions hazardous to small craft through at least Thursday 
afternoon in Tinian and Saipan waters. However, seas may briefly 
drop below 10 feet Tuesday night as winds slow and some swells 
decrease, before another resurgence in the monsoon surge brings seas 
back up Wednesday. When said monsoon surge returns, sea conditions 
hazardous to small craft may return to Guam and Rota waters in the 
second half of the week. Hazardous surf and a high risk of rip 
currents are expected to continue along west and north facing reefs 
through Thursday afternoon, as northwesterly and northeasterly swells
continue to mix in the region.

Tropical Systems...
Tropical Storm Peilou (formerly Kujira) continues to move at a fast
pace, away from the Marianas, with it's current location near 21N151E
(roughly 300 miles northeast of the Maug Islands). This system will
not be a factor in our weather, aside from the persistent west to
southwest surface winds across the Marianas.

Then we have Invest 90W (rated as "Sub-Low" from JTWC - the Joint
Typhoon warning Center), and it's located northeast of Kwajalein
(near 10.5N 169.4E). 90W continues to move very slowly, with both the
GEFS and ECENS having trouble locking onto the tropical disturbance.
There's elevated convection near the western semicircle of the 
circulation, and brief surface-based attempts south-southeast of the
LLCC. The GEFS and ECENS both show this system remaining 
disorganized with their solutions reforming a center near 8N151E in 
about 6 days. It'll be interesting to watch, as the MJO (Madden- 
Julian Oscillation) will be in a favorable location. It's several 
days out though, so plenty of time to watch it, as even a week out 
it's not forecast as any significant circulation. We'll keep an eye 
on it though over the next several days.

Eastern Micronesia...
Invest 90W continues to show improved westerly inflow, with an
elevated disturbance located on it's southwest to west flank. This
along with the inflow is allowing for numerous to widespread shower
and thunderstorm development to affect Kosrae, and it'll move into
Pohnpei's area within the next 24 hours. As such, rainfall
potential/shower coverage was increased at both locations. Kosrae
also remains under a High Surf Advisory for the south-facing reefs,
as a pulse of energy south of the equator augments swell heights to 
hazardous levels. This will continue through early Wednesday morning 
at the very least, and this threat may persist a little longer. 
We'll keep an eye out for that potential. As for Majuro, isolated to 
widely-scattered showers and perhaps a thunderstorm is all you can 
look for over the next several days.

As for marine conditions, mainly light to gentle winds are expected
area-wide, with seas of 5 to 7 feet subsiding a foot for the latter
half of the week.

Western Micronesia...
Satellite observations show mostly clear to partly cloudy skies 
across western Micronesia. Altimetry shows combined seas between 4 
and 7 feet. 

Overall, minimal changes were made with this forecast package. The 
status quo will continue for Palau and Yap through the period with 
surface ridging remaining in place. Yap could see some 20 PoPs 
through Tuesday, but shower coverage is expected to remain isolated. 
For Chuuk, an increase in showers is expected as the surface high 
pressure shifts westward. Current satellite obs show an increasing 
agitated cumulus field developing across Chuuk. Isolated showers are 
expected to become scattered overnight. A relative lull in showers 
activity is expected Wednesday and Thursday before increased shower 
coverage returns towards the end of the week. This will be the 
leading wave of a pattern change that looks to shake up the weather 
across eastern Yap State just beyond the forecast period. 

Combined seas are between 5 and 7 feet across western Micronesia and 
seas are expected to fall 1 to 2 feet over the coming days. Benign 
marine conditions will prevail through the forecast period.
